title: Commit messages and the Conventional Commits standard

videos.script: Here is a history. Update. Changes. Fix. Work in progress. Fixed stuff. And my favourite, asdf. {{bad}} Every one of those commits was a real change, made for a real reason, by somebody who knew exactly why at the time. And every reason is gone. {{gone}} The message is the one place a commit says why. The code shows what changed. The date shows when, the author shows who. Only the message can say what problem it solved, and it is the only part most people will ever read, one line at a time, in a log. {{why}} This lesson is how to write that line so it still makes sense in a year. {{line}} And it is about a convention many teams adopt, conventional commits, where the first word of the message says what kind of change it is, so that a program can read the history too, and write the release notes. {{convention}} Good messages come from good commits, so the lesson ends with how to shape the commits themselves before anybody sees them. {{title}}
